title: uBASIC — libre line-numbered BASIC that RUNS on the 8086 (DOS)
notes: uBASIC is a tiny line-numbered BASIC interpreter in portable C, BSD-3-Clause (Copyright (c) 2006 Adam Dunkels; 2013 Danyil Bohdan). UNLIKE ACK (a host cross-compiler whose OUTPUT runs on the 8086), UBASIC.EXE is ITSELF a 16-bit MS-DOS program: it runs on the bw-board 8086 DOS service layer, reads a BASIC program from PROG.BAS via INT 21h file I/O (open/read), and prints via the C library (INT 21h/INT 10h). It is the DOS-NATIVE complement to Small-C -- a libre BASIC that runs ON the machine, not merely one whose output does. Two small changes over upstream (see fetch.sh + dosmain.c): VARIABLE_TYPE widened char->int (16-bit ints), and a PROG.BAS-reading DOS front-end replacing upstream's hardcoded-program use-ubasic.c. Built with ia16-elf-gcc; the GPL of that GCC port is a BUILD-time tool only (the shipped binary links newlib + libi86, both permissive). Proven on the bench: `10 print 6*7` -> `42`, and demo.bas exercises GOSUB/FOR-NEXT/LET/IF-THEN. Verified in brickwright-lite's test/dos-compile.test.mjs, which runs UBASIC.EXE on the real DOS bench (createDos8086 loadExe + INT 21h) with PROG.BAS mounted and asserts 42. In lite it is wired as runDosToolchain('ubasic', source) and the code tab's 'BASIC (uBASIC on DOS)' profile. The run-dos CLI mounts the program via `--file PROG.BAS=samples/answer.bas --variant 80186` (note: the CLI can drop piped stdout on process.exit; the bench harness / lite test is the authoritative capture).
